question: Two cyclists start from the same place and go in opposite directions. One goes towards the north at the speed of 14 Km/h and the other goes towards the south at 21 Km/h. How long do they take to be 43.75 Km apart?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in opposite directions = Sum of individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 14 + 21 = 35 km/h.

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 43.75 ÷ 35 = 1.25 hours.

Convert to minutes: 1.25 × 60 = 75 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 75 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Cyclist 1** (North) = 14 km/h

Speed of **Cyclist 2** (South) = 21 km/h

Required **Distance** apart = 43.75 km

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a509ae7990b1bfb89b25969a52779c3d3f1e52291d32ceded15768ae1f5539c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 14 + 21 = 35 km/h

⇒ Time required in hours = 43.75 ÷ 35

⇒ Time = 1.25 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 1.25 × 60

⇒ Time = 75 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 75 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is the **sum** of their speeds (u + v). When they move in the **same direction**, it is the **difference** (u − v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **hours to minutes**, multiply by 60.

Basic Formula

Distance = Speed × Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed = Distance ÷ Time.</p
